samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small lock: a single thin dark corridor of constant width that bends about but never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself. A solid dark round bead sits at one end of the corridor, and the walk starts at that bead and follows the corridor to its far end. Coloured marks sit directly on the corridor, and each is one of two kinds: a small filled round disk is a key, and a straight narrow bar laid across the corridor is a gate. Keys and gates are coloured red, green, blue or purple. Walking from the bead, every key that is met is picked up and kept for the rest of the walk. A gate can be passed only if a key of that same colour has already been picked up earlier along the corridor; a key of the gate's colour that lies further along the corridor is too late to help. The walk stops at the first gate it cannot pass, and there is always such a gate. Only the order of the marks along the corridor matters, not how far apart they are. The lock may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside the corridor is inert decoration. What colour is the gate where the walk stops? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.
